title: Main Idea — Skill Check
description: Identify the central idea and distinguish it from supporting details.
subject: rla
author: Chee Skool
reviewNotes: Unseen independent check; no hints, retries, or guided scaffolding.

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?

options.text: Westhaven replaced reliance on one warning method with a layered, location-specific alert system
Why outdoor sirens should be removed from every town
options.whyWrong: The siren remains part of Westhaven’s system.

options.text: How residents can repair phones before storms
options.whyWrong: Phone repair is not the passage’s focus.

options.text: Why local radio is the only reliable flood-warning tool
options.whyWrong: The passage emphasizes several channels, not one.

explanation.whyCorrect: This choice matches the passage without adding or changing what the text says.
explanation.quickTip: Use only what the passage actually supports.

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of the second paragraph?

options.text: Community volunteers now control all evacuation decisions
options.whyWrong: Volunteers translate messages; officials manage the system.

options.text: The fire department stopped using evacuation zones
Westhaven added several ways to deliver the same zone-specific warnings
Residents must choose only one warning channel
options.whyWrong: The layered system intentionally uses multiple channels.

explanation.whyCorrect: This choice matches the passage without adding or changing what the text says.
explanation.quickTip: Use only what the passage actually supports.

questions.prompt: Why does the author mention phones losing power, sleeping radio listeners, and hard-to-hear sirens?

options.text: To argue that warning systems are not worth funding
options.whyWrong: The passage supports improving warnings, not abandoning them.

options.text: To show that residents are responsible for every warning failure
options.whyWrong: The examples show limits of communication channels.

options.text: To prove that text messages are always fastest
options.whyWrong: Phones are also described as having limits.

options.text: To explain why relying on several channels is more dependable than relying on one

explanation.whyCorrect: This choice matches the passage without adding or changing what the text says.
explanation.quickTip: Use only what the passage actually supports.

questions.prompt: Which title best reflects the passage as a whole?

options.text: The End of Westhaven’s River Siren
One Warning Is Not Enough: Building a Layered Flood-Alert System
Three Languages Spoken in Westhaven
options.whyWrong: Translation is one feature, not the whole focus.

options.text: How to Read a Fire Department Map
options.whyWrong: The map is only one part of the system.

explanation.whyCorrect: This choice matches the passage without adding or changing what the text says.
explanation.quickTip: Use only what the passage actually supports.

questions.prompt: Which detail is most important to the passage’s main idea?

options.text: The system repeats location-specific warnings through texts, sirens, radio, translations, and a map
The original siren was near the town center
options.whyWrong: That is background explaining the old system.

options.text: Some residents sleep while the radio is on
options.whyWrong: The passage says radio listeners may be asleep, but this is one limitation.

options.text: The first review occurs after a storm season
options.whyWrong: This is a follow-up step, not the central idea.

explanation.whyCorrect: This choice matches the passage without adding or changing what the text says.
explanation.quickTip: Use only what the passage actually supports.

questions.prompt: What broader idea does the passage most strongly imply about emergency communication?

options.text: A new technology should always replace an older one completely
options.whyWrong: Westhaven keeps the siren while adding other channels.

options.text: Messages should avoid naming specific locations
options.whyWrong: The new system becomes more location-specific.

options.text: Different communication methods can cover one another’s weaknesses
Resident surveys are more important than delivery records
options.whyWrong: Officials plan to compare both kinds of information.

explanation.whyCorrect: This choice matches the passage without adding or changing what the text says.
explanation.quickTip: Use only what the passage actually supports.
